data.title: Shifted by three
story: The security team hid a practice flag with a Caesar cipher: every letter is shifted 3 places forward (A becomes D, B becomes E).
Use the Python console to shift every letter 3 places back, then type the flag.
data.scratch:
message = "IODJ{NHHS_OHDUQLQJ}"
result = ""
for letter in message:
    result = result + letter
print(result)

explanation: A Caesar cipher is undone by shifting each letter back: ord() turns a letter into a number, subtract 3, then chr() turns it back into a letter. A cipher like this is easy to crack, so it is never used to protect real data.
hints: First try ord("I") - 3 in the console. Which letter does chr() give?
Only the letters A to Z are shifted; the { } and _ signs stay the same.
